description:
We are an interdisciplinary team passionate about space exploration, creativity, and innovation. Our team brings together skills in graphic design, aerospace engineering, software development, 3D modeling, and scientific research.

We work collaboratively to transform complex scientific ideas into engaging visual and interactive experiences. By combining technical knowledge with creative thinking, we aim to make space science more accessible, educational, and inspiring for everyone.
summary:
ECHOES – The Forgotten Explorers is an interactive, bilingual educational website developed in response to NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026: “Abandoned but not Forgotten: Storytelling about NASA's Discarded Equipment on the Moon and Mars.”

Our project explores the stories of spacecraft, rovers, landers, and scientific equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars. Through dedicated artifact pages, interactive exploration sections, a mission timeline, and a fleet archive, we present the history of these machines, their missions, scientific purposes, achievements, and current status in an engaging and accessible way.

ECHOES addresses the challenge by transforming forgotten space hardware into meaningful stories, helping people understand that these objects are not simply abandoned machines, but important parts of humanity's journey in space exploration. The project is important because it preserves the legacy of past missions, highlights their scientific and technological contributions, and makes space exploration history easier for everyone to discover and learn from.
details:
Project Details — ECHOES: The Forgotten Explorers

ECHOES is an interactive, bilingual educational website that tells the stories of spacecraft, rovers, landers, and scientific equipment left on the Moon and Mars after their missions. Our goal is to make these often-overlooked parts of space exploration easier and more interesting for the public to discover.

The website organizes information into several sections. The Home page introduces the project and invites visitors to explore the Moon and Mars. The Explore section allows users to browse the archive and filter items by location and category. The Fleet section presents 14 spacecraft and scientific instruments, with brief descriptions and additional details for each item. The Timeline displays important events from lunar and Martian missions in chronological order. The About section explains the project's mission and goals and includes a glossary of scientific terms, frequently asked questions (FAQ), and a library of research sources.

ECHOES is designed to make learning more accessible through Arabic and English language support, an organized browsing experience, interactive filters, and a visually engaging space-themed interface. Users can discover what each piece of equipment was designed to do, learn about its mission, and understand its scientific contributions.

The intended impact is to raise awareness of the history of space exploration, preserve the stories of forgotten equipment, and encourage curiosity about space science, technology, and engineering. By bringing information together in one place, ECHOES helps students and the general public explore these stories without needing advanced scientific knowledge.

We developed the website using HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript, with Google Fonts for typography. HTML structures the content, CSS controls the visual design and responsive layout, and JavaScript supports interactive features and language switching. The website is designed to work through a web browser on both mobile devices and computers.

For research, we consulted official and scientific resources, including NASA Science, NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL), NASA Goddard, and other relevant mission references. We included a sources section to help visitors explore the original information.

The creative aspect of ECHOES is its storytelling approach: instead of focusing only on famous missions and discoveries, we give attention to the equipment that remains after missions end. We combined educational information with an interactive archive, a chronological timeline, and a bilingual interface to create an engaging learning experience.

Throughout development, our team considered scientific accuracy, accessibility, ease of navigation, bilingual content, and compatibility with different screen sizes. ECHOES is an independent educational project created for the NASA Space Apps Challenge and is not an official NASA website or affiliated with NASA.
